title: I tried coding my game for 3 years then I tried Claude Code
author: Maximum_Reward_7575
selftext:
3 years ago while trying to sleep I thought what if every move in a game was a visible Dice roll that you could try to bend? 

Struggled a LOT with coding all this, then I tried Claude Code and was able to finally create the game I had in mind.

I've changed and experimented with a LOT of mechanics over the years, so I'd especially love to hear which ones feel good/bad to play.

Hope you enjoy it! 

[https://leseau.itch.io/dice-odyssey](https://leseau.itch.io/dice-odyssey)

comments.author: Nearby_Ad4786
comments.body: I realle love the scenario art, but the UI doesnt match with it. Good job !!

replies.author: Maximum_Reward_7575
replies.body: Thanks! Can you tell me a bit more which parts exactly feel the most off to you?

replies.author: Nearby_Ad4786
replies.body: Well the background is using a cartoon minmalist style. The cards and dice are using more detailed textures and details. You can just share the sprites and background to your AI and ask for their visual style to replicate it

replies.author: Maximum_Reward_7575
replies.body: Yeah I get what you mean. I find it pretty hard to have a cohesive visual style, AIs tend to do their thing. Is there a specific kind of prompt / settings / workflow you'd recommend? Thanks for the feedback!

replies.author: Nearby_Ad4786
replies.body: Just that. Take an image as visual refference. Describe it with AI. Make a prompt that has all the generic info that u want in your assets. Use the prompt in each generation

replies.author: Maximum_Reward_7575
replies.body: I'll try to get better dice textures yeah they're probably too detailed atm. Thanks!

replies.author: Calm-Chip-8039
replies.body: Whay AI do you use to generate art?  Im having trouble finding a way to generate ui/2d elements because i cant get them on a transparent background.  I end up having to try to cut them out and it looks janky

replies.author: Maximum_Reward_7575
replies.body:
Mostly gpt image 2. I used to use remove bg but also had janky results even when using white background, no background, ...

My solution is to ask Claude which background will make his job easy (usually magenta or solid green). Then, Claude can actually remove the background for you. It sometimes takes a few tries but keep pointing what's off and he'll eventually fix it. Overkill with Fable if he's struggling a lot.

Oh and you need Python installed and connected because Claude actually writes a Python script for that. Super worth it!

replies.author: Ok-Adhesiveness7433
replies.body: If you have the specs to do a little local work. I’d suggest a more powerful tool to remove the background bud. AI Gen Studio is free and has a bunch of neat tools you can use. COMFYUI has a built in image remover that keeps removes the background while adhering to the preservation of RGBD.

comments.author: Sea_Advance273
comments.body: How fast did development accelerate with Claude compared to doing it yourself? It took me about 1 year to create the game I wanted to with coding agents but I'm convinced it would have taken me 10 years without lol. But this was with the agents from 1 year ago, I'm pretty sure with modern agents and my refined workflow I could now make it in mere days.

replies.author: Maximum_Reward_7575
replies.body:
Oh yeah definitely would have been able to recreate the game in a much, much faster time haha. My programming skills are not that great and I learnt Godot by working on this project so there was a lot of spaghetti code and frustrating issues.

The greatest thing Claude Code brought is that I can now add many features I had in mind without thinking about the technical struggle and time it would take me. For example I had the dice infusion (modify your dice abilities) in mind for months but thought I'll do it later, it's gonna take a good week. Well... 2 prompts lol.

replies.author: Maximum_Reward_7575
replies.body:
Thanks a lot!

I love TW but never played the board game. Did some quick research and I also see dice and odds manipulation. Can you tell me a bit more? Please tell me my game doesn't already exist somewhere haha

replies.author: Infinitecontextlabs
replies.body:
It is very close to the mechanics of the board game but different enough that it doesn't feel copied. Either way, the game I'm developing is based off that style so I was just seeing ways your system would actually be better suited for my game world.

We should chat in DM

replies.author: Maximum_Reward_7575
replies.body: Interesting, thanks. Of course, you're welcome! :)
